event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: WST’s 10-K squarely positions the COVID-19 pandemic as a recent, still-evolving threat that can directly impair virtually every layer of the enterprise—operations, supply chain continuity, workforce availability, distribution logistics, cost structure and customer demand patterns.  The discussion is forward-looking but anchored in already-observed impacts (higher expenses, government travel bans, demand swings), and therefore blends realised and potential risk.  Language is specific: it calls out raw-material shortages, transportation bottlenecks, employee illness, and unpredictable demand shifts—exactly the vectors most companies faced in 2020-21.  No quantified dollar loss is given on the risk side, but the company admits that expenses have already risen and that ultimate effects are “beyond our knowledge or control,” underscoring materiality.  Mitigations are mentioned only in passing; thus aggravating factors dominate.  Because the filing date (23 Feb 2021) is well within three years of the WHO’s pandemic declaration (11 Mar 2020), the Time Decay Principle allows high—but not automatically maximum—scores.  Overall, the evidence points to a high, active risk environment with limited offsetting controls, justifying upper-mid to high micro-scores across the extracted sentences.

evidence_list.snippet: Our results of operations and financial condition may be adversely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and other public health epidemics.

components.reason: Explicitly links COVID-19 to potential adverse effects on operations and financial condition.
Specifies the pandemic by name, showing direct relevance.
Uses the cautious word “may,” signalling uncertainty and reducing immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear acknowledgement of pandemic threat to core performance but phrased as a possibility, yielding a solid mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: Our results of operations and financial condition may be adversely affected if the progression of the COVID-19 pandemic interferes with our ability, or that of our employees, contractors, suppliers, customers and other business partners, to carry out and deliver on business obligations.

components.reason: Details multiple stakeholder groups potentially disrupted (employees, contractors, suppliers, customers).
Connects interference with business obligations to adverse financial impact.
Forward-looking ‘may’ softens certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds concrete supply-chain and labour dimensions, boosting severity, but still framed as conditional.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 may have an adverse effect on our operations, supply chains and distribution systems.

components.reason: Specifically names operations, supply chains and distribution as vulnerable areas.
Directly attributes risk to COVID-19.
Use of ‘may’ indicates possibility rather than current impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies three critical functions but remains brief and hypothetical, so score is modest.

evidence_list.snippet: Known potential impacts are illness in our workforce as well as a reduction in access to raw materials for production and access to transportation of product.

components.reason: Cites employee illness—a direct labour shortage risk.
Mentions reduced access to raw materials—supply risk.
Mentions reduced access to transportation—logistics risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Enumerates three concrete, severe operational pinch-points, warranting a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: There could be other unknown and unforeseeable impacts.

components.reason: Admits existence of additional, unspecified risks, highlighting uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Very generic acknowledgement of uncertainty; minimal incremental severity.

evidence_list.snippet: These impacts have increased and may continue to increase our expenses, including costs associated with preventive and precautionary measures that we, companies with which we conduct business and governments are taking.

components.reason: States that expenses have already risen—evidence of realised financial impact.
Signals ongoing cost escalation (‘may continue’).
Links costs to broad external preventive measures beyond company control.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows actual expense hit plus continuing pressure, driving a high recent-event score.

evidence_list.snippet: Government measures include actions that restrict or prohibit travel, which in turn may impact our operations by limiting our employees’ ability to come to work, or the employees of companies upon which our supply chain depends.

components.reason: Specifies government travel bans as external risk driver.
Ties directly to workforce availability and supplier labour constraints.
Conditional language ‘may impact’ reduces certainty slightly.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights regulatory-induced labour shortages, but framed as potential, not realised.

evidence_list.snippet: The impacts of the pandemic and the aforesaid measures taken by other companies and governments may cause us to experience significant and unpredictable reductions or increases in demand for certain of our products.

components.reason: Addresses demand volatility—fundamental market risk.
Qualifies the swing as ‘significant and unpredictable,’ emphasising severity.
Use of ‘may’ denotes possibility, tempering immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures major revenue-side uncertainty, but still hypothetical, so score is upper-mid.

evidence_list.snippet: This is especially possible in the event customers re-prioritize their needs due to the changing environment.

components.reason: Links demand risk to customer behaviour shifts during pandemic.
Phrase ‘especially possible’ keeps it speculative.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds minimal new risk information; largely a speculative qualifier, resulting in a near-zero increment.

evidence_list.snippet: Despite our efforts to manage these COVID-19 related risks, their ultimate impact on the Company will be determined by factors beyond our knowledge or control, including the duration of COVID-19 and further actions taken to control its spread and mitigate its public health effects.

components.reason: Acknowledges uncontrollable external drivers (pandemic duration, government action).
Admits current risk-management efforts may not suffice.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concedes limited control over outcome, reinforcing residual risk but without quantifying severity.

evidence_list.snippet: The functioning of our manufacturing and distribution assets and systems could be disrupted for reasons either within or beyond our control, including, without limitation: extreme weather or longer-term climatic changes; natural disasters; pandemic; war; accidental damage; disruption to the supply of material or services; product quality and safety issues; systems failure; workforce actions; or environmental matters.

components.reason: Lists ‘pandemic’ among disruption triggers, confirming operational vulnerability.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic catch-all clause; pandemic merely one of many factors, so incremental score is low.

evidence_list.snippet: Proprietary Products gross profit margin increased by 2.8 margin points in 2020, due to a favorable mix of products sold, production efficiencies, and sales price increases, partially offset by increased overhead costs including compensation costs and COVID-19 related expenses.

components.reason: Confirms COVID-19 has already driven overhead cost increases.
Offsets noted by overall margin improvement and other positive factors.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows realised cost pressure from COVID-19 but tempered by positive margin effects, yielding a modest net risk score.
